starting_image.description: Path to existing ext2 image to use as starting point.

root_dirs.description: List of source directories to add to filesystem root (or subpaths). Each entry maps to `-d` option. The optional `dest` is the target path within the image (defaults to root '/').

root_dirs.items.dest.description: Target path within image (e.g., `/bin`, `.` for root).

devtables.description: List of device table spec files, each with optional target path. Each entry maps to `-D` option.

devtables.items.src.description: Path to spec file on host.

devtables.items.dest.description: Target path within image for table entries (e.g., `/dev`).

tarballs.description: List of tarball archives to extract, with optional target path. Each entry maps to `-a` option.

tarballs.items.src.description: Path to tarball archive on host.

tarballs.items.dest.description: Target path within image where archive contents are extracted.

block_size.description: Filesystem block size in bytes (must be power of 2 and multiple of 1024).

number_of_inodes.description: Maximum number of inodes (0 means auto-calculate from available blocks).

volume_label.description: Volume label for the ext2 filesystem (max 16 chars).

bytes_per_inode.description: Ratio of bytes per inode when auto-calculating inode count.

reserved_percentage.description: Percentage of blocks reserved for root (0 prevents 'lost+found' directory).

creator_os.description: Value for creator OS field in superblock (e.g., LINUX, HURD).

block_map_path.description: Path to write a block map file for this path in the image.

fill_value.description: Fill value (0-255) for unallocated blocks (0 = zero-fill).

allow_holes.description: Enable creation of files with holes (sparse files).

faketime.description: Use timestamp 0 for inode and filesystem creation (for reproducibility).

squash_uids.description: Squash UIDs/GIDs to root:root for `-d`-added files.

squash_perms.description: Squash permissions for `-d`-added files (analogous to umask 077).

verbose.description: Print resulting filesystem structure to stdout.

output_image.description: Output image path. Use '-' for stdout.
